trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
Going up-left would leave number 2 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going down-left, the next 6 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at number 6. So the line goes down-right.
Going left, the next 5 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at number 6. So the line goes down-left.
Going up-left would strand number 4: it would be left with only one free neighbour; going down-right would turn number 4 into a dead-end pocket with no way out. So the line goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down-left.
Going down-left would force the line onto number 10 before its turn. So the line goes left.
Going down-right would force the line onto number 10 before its turn; going down-left would leave number 7 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes up-left.
I can't rule out left or up-left yet, so I'll make an educated guess: left.
Going up-right would leave number 7 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going down-left leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes left.
Going up-left would cut off the top edge (13 cells); going left would cut off the bottom-left corner (12 cells). So the line goes down-right.
Going down-left would force the line onto number 12 before its turn. So the line goes right.
Going down-right, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at number 9. So the line goes down-left.
Going left would leave both number 12 and number 11 needing the line next, and it can't do both; going down-right would force the line onto number 11 before its turn. So the line goes right.
Going down-left would force the line onto number 11 before its turn; going down-right would cut off the bottom edge (3 cells). So the line goes right.

Going down-left would leave both cell (-2,3) and cell (0,3) needing the line next, and it can't do both; going down-right would turn number 10 into a dead-end pocket with no way out. So the line goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down-left.
Going right would leave both number 14 and number 15 needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes up-right.
The line must go down-right: right is number 20, which comes later.
Going down-right would turn number 15 into a dead-end pocket with no way out. So the line goes down-left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Going up-right would wall in number 20, the last number. So the line goes down-right.
Going right would turn number 18 into a dead-end pocket with no way out. So the line goes down-right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up-right.
Cell (3,-3) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes up-right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
